key_idea: The number of digits of n! equals floor(sum log10 i)+1 and is strictly increasing once n>=10, so the length of the input identifies n; tiny inputs are compared by value.
sketch: If the input has at most 10 digits, parse it and multiply up until the factorial matches (needed because 0!/1! and 5!/6! etc. share digit counts). Otherwise accumulate log10 in long double and return the first n whose digit count reaches the input length. n is at most about 205022 for 10^6 digits, so it is O(n). Pitfall: floating error near integer logs, hence long double and no reliance on exact equality; reading a 10^6 character token needs a large buffer.
